title: Pixel-verified fast-rotating old M dwarfs from TESS full-frame images have no CPVs where contraction alone predicts 5.3; at fixed corotation ratio their CPV rate is below 0.37 of the young rate
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, fast-rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. A frozen contraction-only model, in which the CPV rate depends only on x = R_cor/R*, predicts CPVs among old main-sequence M dwarfs at the x of young hosts. Earlier cleaned samples could not decide (3 seen, 6.4 predicted, p = 0.15). We built a deeper sample from the TESS All-Sky Rotation Survey (TARS): 3,100 old M dwarfs within 150 pc with periods below 0.3 d. We read 5x5-pixel 200-s cutouts (sectors 56-109) from the MAST FFI cubes, used the source pipeline, located each signal with a Gaia-scene pixel test, measured each star's efficiency by injection of young-CPV templates, and labelled curves blind. A pre-registration fixed the tests before processing. Of 438 old rapid rotators in the model window, 349 signals come from other stars and 65 are on target (21 at x < 3.5, 17 of them new). Among the 65, the model predicts 5.32 CPVs (4.05-6.98); we observe 0 (p = 0.006); the old/young rate factor is below 0.37. Combined with the earlier independent samples: 3 seen, 9.66 predicted, p = 0.025, factor 0.31 (0.07-0.86). A positive control with young 1-24 Myr stars gives observed/predicted 1.27 (0.77-2.01), and injection efficiency matches same-sector recovery of known CPVs. Seventeen variants give p = 0.001-0.042 except a small dMG < 0 subset (0.097). Thus contraction alone does not explain the low CPV rate of old stars; a second age-dependent factor, such as material supply, field structure or close binarity, is necessary. Limitations: about 5 predicted CPVs, one automated vetter, an extrapolated young model, and a simple PRF.
